title: [YouPass Collect] - Forests and timber
prompt: The charts give information about world forests in five different regions. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The given pie charts illustrate the percentage of forests in 5 different regions globally, and their timber production.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Despite being covered with similar areas of woodland, Africa and North America stand at the two ends of the timber production spectrum, with the former being the smallest and the latter being the largest global producers of timber.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Although Africa has the largest forested areas in the world (27%), its lumber output is the lowest, at only 9% of the global production. In contrast, North America, with 30% of the market share, is the premiere producer of timber, while only having the second largest forested area, at exactly one-fourth of the entire world.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: The next largest timber manufacturers are South America, Europe, and Asia, in that order, with their figures ranging from 23% to 18%. Of these 3 continents, Europe has the largest area of wooded land, at 18%, which is respectively 2% higher than that of South America and 4% higher than that of Asia.
